material_definitions: Solid electrolytes based on lithium titanium phosphate (LiTi2(PO4)3) were prepared.
The materials belong to the Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 system (M3+=Al3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, Fe3+, Sc3+, In3+, Lu3+, Y3+, and La3+).
The conductivity enhancement is primarily attributed to the increase of the sintered pellet density and the enhancement of the lithium concentration at the grain boundaries.
The maximum conductivity was achieved by partially replacing Ti4+ in LiTi2(PO4)3 with M3+ (specifically Al3+ and Sc3+) at a composition of x=0.3.
Solid electrolytes based on lithium titanium phosphate (LiTi2(PO4)3) were prepared.
The materials belong to the Li(1+x)M(x)Ti(2-x)(PO4)3 system (M3+=Al3+, Cr3+, Ga3+, Fe3+, Sc3+, In3+, Lu3+, Y3+, and La3+).
The conductivity enhancement is primarily attributed to the increase of the sintered pellet density and the enhancement of the lithium concentration at the grain boundaries.
The maximum conductivity was achieved by partially replacing Ti4+ in LiTi2(PO4)3 with M3+ (specifically Al3+ and Sc3+) at a composition of x=0.3.
The study focuses on lithium titanium phosphate (LiTi2(PO4)3) based solid electrolytes.
The material series involves partial substitution of P5+ with Si4+ or Ti4+ with M3+ (e.g., Al or Sc) to enhance conductivity.
Conductivity enhancement also resulted from mixing binders such as Li2O or Li4P2O7 with LiTi2(PO4)3, primarily leading to better densification.
These conductors exhibit high lithium ionic conductivity even at room temperature and stability in air.
